elements.element: The Agreement is governed by the laws of the State of New York.
elements.evidence: Section 28.1 expressly provides that the Agreement is governed by the laws of the State of New York.

elements.element: The state courts located in New York County, New York have jurisdiction.
elements.evidence: Section 28.2 designates the state courts located in New York County, New York.

elements.element: The federal courts located in New York County, New York have jurisdiction.
elements.evidence: Section 28.2 designates the federal courts located in New York County, New York.

elements.element: Jurisdiction of the designated New York County state and federal courts is exclusive.
elements.evidence: Although Section 28.2 initially states that those courts have exclusive jurisdiction, its final sentence permits either Party to seek temporary injunctive relief concerning confidential information or intellectual property in another court. This is an operative exception to exclusivity.

elements.element: The governing law is Delaware law, California law, or the laws of England and Wales.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause selects New York law, not any of the listed fallback governing laws.

elements.element: If Delaware law is selected, the designated courts are in Delaware.
elements.evidence: The condition is demonstrably absent because the rendered clause selects New York law rather than Delaware law.

elements.element: If California law is selected, the designated courts are in California.
elements.evidence: The condition is demonstrably absent because the rendered clause selects New York law rather than California law.

elements.element: If the laws of England and Wales are selected, the designated courts are in London.
elements.evidence: The condition is demonstrably absent because the rendered clause selects New York law rather than the laws of England and Wales.

result.reason: The redline correctly changes the governing law to New York and resolves the conflict between Sections 28.1 and 28.2. However, the express right to seek temporary injunctive relief in any other court with jurisdiction prevents the New York County courts from having unqualified exclusive jurisdiction. No complete preferred or fallback level is therefore achieved. The drafting is otherwise coherent, but it does not implement the stated exclusive-forum requirement and the margin comment overlooks the operative carveout.
